messages.subject: GPCM Standard Error
parts:
Hi Phil,

I've been using the github dev version for getting the standard errors, thanks for adding this option!

So when calling:

x2r <- mirt(fr2, 1, itemtype='gpcm', SE=TRUE)
coef(x2r, printSE=TRUE)

for some estimated coefficients the standard errors are NaN, do you have any ideas why is that?

Thank you very much!
Cheers,
Olivia

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: GPCM Standard Error
parts:
Hi Olivia,

The issue is that the information matrix estimated from the S-EM algorithm is not positive definite. Therefore when it is inverted to find the large sample parameter covariance matrix some of the diagonal terms become negative (negative variance of course make no sense). Unfortunately this has little to do with the model itself, and has more to do with the imprecision in the S-EM algorithm for building the observed information matrix (inspect x2r@information to see what I mean, at the very least you'll notice the matrix isn't symmetric, which in itself is an issue). NaN is a place-holder indication the parameter variance was less than 0, and therefore not defined. 

Currently there are only 3 SE.types that behave well under regular conditions, 'BL', 'Fisher', and 'crossprod'. I don't find it necessarily troubling though, since you could always bootstrap your model with boot.mirt() to obtain SE's that way, or estimate only the NaN parameters using a profile-likelihood approach via PCLI.mirt(). It's more just annoying, and has given me questions on whether I should provide an option to smooth this matrix before computing the standard errors. 

When the S-EM algorithm works it works well, otherwise you have to resort to other methods to patch it up. Hope that helps.

Phil
